alignments.note: Rule 86: the participle carries subordination, so the supplied *though* is its helper; the supplied complement *in him* is likewise licensed by the participle. Rule 15 permits the discontinuity, and marking *in him* added remains defensible.
Genitive with its case preposition on the noun.

The apodosis marker *yet* answers to the concessive construction and rides with the finite verb it introduces. The supplied *of* is English verb government over a bare accusative object and no Greek preposition stands, so it is a rule 7 helper on the verb that licenses it, exactly as *for* is at ACT.13.21 (ᾐτήσαντο βασιλέα -> *they asked for a king*); rule 21's case-preposition clause reaches an oblique case, which the accusative Πιλᾶτον is not. Leaving *of* on the name, as the accepted reading did, is the competing analysis.
The accusative person asked stands bare; the supplied *of* belongs to the verb.
The accusative subject of the infinitive becomes the subject of the ASV's finite clause.
Rule 85: the supplied complementizer belongs to the infinitive the ASV expands into a finite clause.

review_notes: Corrected the placement of the supplied *of* before Πιλᾶτον: it is now the verb's rule 7 helper rather than a case preposition on the name, matching ACT.13.21's identical ᾐτήσαντο with an accusative object. Only the boundary between the ᾐτήσαντο and Πιλᾶτον units changed; no status, head or other unit is affected.

The chapter's 'case preposition stays with the name' convention is retained where the case is oblique, as at ACT.13.23's dative τῷ Ἰσραήλ -> *unto Israel*, and at this verse's own genitive θανάτου -> *of death*.
